summary: Canary fallback routed traffic to initializing replica causing p95/p99 spikes and intermittent timeouts
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC, ClipStream observed a large increase in tail latency (p95/p99) and recurring client timeouts (504/524) for text generation requests. Impact: Production traffic for their dedicated deployment experienced spikes in per-request latency and occasional 5xx responses, degrading user-facing ingestion pipelines. Environment: prod, us-east. Initial triage indicated the platform routed a subset of requests to a canary variant that was still initializing, producing cold-start delays and failed requests. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and follow-up actions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady client traffic to ClipStream production route (tokenized chat completion workload, ~15 req/s per client).
2) Trigger platform canary rollout for model variant redwood/fp16-compat-7b-canary-2026-03 with default fallback policy (weight-based, allow-initializing).
3) Observe backend routing decisions and per-request latency for requests redirected to the canary variant.
4) Note intermittent 504/524 from gateway and increased p95/p99 on request traces that hit initializing replicas.
observed_behavior: - Around 09:10 UTC, p95 increased from ~120ms to ~1.8s and p99 hit 6-8s for the customer route.
- 1.2% of requests returned 5xx (mix of 504 and 524) during the peak period.
- Traces show requests routed to a variant with logs indicating 'variant_state=initializing' and long kernel load times (cold-start).
- Autoscaler attempted to spin up replicas but new pods remained 'initializing' for ~45-90s due to model quantization hotload.
metrics_snapshot: Customer route: total_rps: 220 -> 210 (steady), error_rate: 0.2% -> 1.2% during incident
Platform: route_fallbacks: 18 per minute to canary variant during 09:10-09:40 UTC
logs: 2026-03-12T09:12:04Z router[smart-routing]: WARN routing-to-variant variant_id=fp16-canary-2026-03 reason=fallback_policy evaluated_weight=0.12 allow_initializing=true
2026-03-12T09:12:04Z api-gateway: ERROR upstream_response=504 upstream_host=10.2.4.19:8080 path=/v1/generate customer=ClipStream
2026-03-12T09:17:22Z autoscaler: INFO requested_replicas=2 pending_provision=2 provider=dedicated-gpu wait_time=65s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: increased latency due to model runtime change in canary causing cold starts. Confirmed: canary image introduced a lazy-quantization step that extends first load time by ~12s per replica.

Routing policy review: smart-routing evaluation allowed 'initializing' variants to receive fallback traffic when stable variants breached latency budget. This behavior is intentional in policy but unsafe for large dedicated customers.
Autoscaler logs show capacity requested but provider API returned delayed GPU provisioning (provider-side laged by ~40s), compounding cold-start impact.

Health checks: readiness probe for canary variant only passes after model weights are fully loaded; during that window some replicas still accepted TCP connections from router because of race in readiness registration.
comments: Maya Patel - 2026-03-12: Customer reported spikes and timeouts, attached trace IDs and replay bundle. Asked for immediate mitigation.
Diego Martinez - 2026-03-12: Scoped to routing + runtime. Reproduced in staging by enabling canary with lazy-quantization. Opening temp rollback for customer pin.

SRE (Evan Li) - 2026-03-12: Provider reported delayed provisioning for GPUs in us-east; working with infra partner to surface capacity metrics. Recommended pinning to stable variant and disabling canary for the route.

Support (Aisha Kumar) - 2026-03-12: Applied customer-side mitigation: pinned ClipStream to redwood/open-llama-7b-v2 and set fallback policy to 'avoid-initializing'. Observed p95 returned to baseline within 6 minutes.

Diego Martinez - 2026-03-13: Confirmed root cause and deployed temporary guard in router to exclude variants with state 'initializing' from fallback selection for high-tier customers. Follow-up ticket created for permanent fix.
resolution: Workaround applied: Pinned ClipStream to stable variant redwood/open-llama-7b-v2 and disabled automatic canary traffic for their route (09:25 UTC).
Temporary platform mitigation: Router guard added to treat 'initializing' variants as ineligible for fallback selection for customers with dedicated/reserved capacity (rolled 09:40 UTC).
Customer impact resolved: p95/p99 returned to normal by ~09:31 UTC after pin + routing guard; no data loss reported.

Permanent follow-ups: INT-4399 created to change fallback policy evaluation to de-prioritize initializing variants globally; INT-4402 created for runtime change to pre-warm quantization layer during rollout; update rollout docs and canary config defaults.
Communication: Sent incident summary and mitigations to customer (ClipStream CS contact) and to #support and #incidents Slack channels with postmortem draft.
